world mission sunday collection thank you for your very generous donations to the mission sunday collection last weekend. €2,001.00 was collected in our parish. thank you! spiritual reflection “today, we face no penal laws. no one is banning the mass. no one is hunting priests. but faith faces a different kind of threat – not persecution, but forgetfulness; not violence, but indifference. the danger now is not that we cannot practice our faith, that we do not bother. the challenge is distraction, busyness and the suggestion that god is optional. and yet – just as in penal times – faith is surviving. it survives in young people searching for meaning. it survives in families rediscovering prayer. it survives in those who go to knock shrine seeking peace and silence. it survives the quiet heart t hat still dares to hope.” (most rev. niall coll, bishop of raphoe) the irish national assembly the synodal assembly took place on saturday, 17th october bringing together nominated lay, clerical and religious delegates from dioceses, parishes, religious congregations, ecclesial movements and other communities from across the church in ireland f or a day of prayer, listening, conversation and discernment to reflect together on the question that has guided the irish synodal pathway since its beginning in 2021: “what does god want from church in ireland at this time?” the irish synodal pathway began in 2021 when the bishops invited the church to embark on a process of renewal inviting people throughout the church to engage in prayer, listening and reflection, and to reflect on important questions about the identity and mis sion of the church in ireland, including its pastoral life, structures, relationships, ministry and place in society. through this process, baptism emerged as a foundational lens understanding the identity and mission of the church, leading to seven priorities: belonging; co-responsibility and lay ministry; family; formation and catechesis; healing; women; and youth. speaking after the assembly, julieann moran, general secretary of the irish synod al pathway, said, “today was an extraordinary moment for the church in ireland, and our task now is to make what happened here at the national synodal assembly an ordinary everyday way of being church at parish level. we came together as the people of god with diverse exp eriences, and we listened to the holy spirit. the path so far has proven that we can do this and can continue to become a synodal church – the church that go d calls us to be.” archbishop eamon martin, archbishop of armagh and president of the irish catholic bishops’ conference, addressed the delegates, saying, “with regard to the particular recommendations made today, it may be that some can be activated easily and quickly. others will greater planning, deployment of resources and personnel. i also hope that initiatives which are already happening around the country can be shared with greater clarity in the light of the momentum coming from today’s assembly.” first holy communion programme we are delighted to welcome next year’s first holy communion candidates and their families to a special enrolment mass at st. john’s church at 6.00pm on next saturday evening . parish ministries we are always eager to expand our parish ministries. if you feel you ar called to share your baptismal gifts by participating in one of our parish ministries – reader, ministry of welcome, music, extraordinary minister of the eucharist – contact the parish office on

including our parishioners, family members, neighbours, friends and all who have no one to remember them. eternal rest grant unto them, o lord, let perpetual light shine upon them. may their souls and all the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of god, rest in peace. amen. november the month of holy souls “it is a holy and wholesome thought to pray for the dead that they may be loosed form their sins.” each november, the church engages in a great crusade of prayer for our dead. we pray for our dead because we believe there is a communion - an unbreakable link - between the living and the dead. that link ensures us that we can help them and they can help us. one saint said that the holy souls may win astounding favours for us and deliver us from evils, sickness and dangers of every kind. our prayer, especially the holy sacrifice of the mass, is the greatest expression of our gratitude and love for those who have died. in fact, the november novena of masses is the most powerful way to honour with great respect the memory of our dead. kilmacow parish priest: fr. martin tobin adm weekend masses : mobile:
